newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's McCully says National a pre-election underdog.
newsitem.headline: NZ's McCully says National a pre-election underdog.

text.p: Cabinet Minister and key party strategist Murray McCully said on Tuesday his National Party Government was the underdog going into the October 12 election.
"The government is very much the underdog I think as far as the polls are concerned, going into the final lap of the election," McCully told a business meeting.

He said National's own polls showed it was three or four percent below what was needed to get more than 50 seats in parliament at the general election, the first to be held under the Mixed Member Proportional (MMP) electoral system.
The battle for Wellington Central, where National's Mark Thomas is up against Act New Zealand's Richard Prebble, was not helping.
National expects Act NZ to be supportive as a potential coalition partner but has accused Act of being slow in the run-up to the campaign.
Opinion polls put National in the lead, but not by enough to win outright under MMP rules, which favour coalitions.
